deep_analysis.executive_intro:
This FTSE screen is broadly neutral: 143 names sit on Hold versus 62 actionable Buys (20 Strong Buy, 42 Buy) and 43 Avoids, so value signals are present but not dominant across the universe. The five highest-ranked Strong Buys cluster in UK cyclicals and income — three Industrials (FirstGroup, ME Group, Morgan Sindall), plus one Healthcare (Hikma) and one Communication Services name (ITV). All five pass every model family (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) with full 20/20 data quality, yet conviction scores are modest (39–53%) because every signal is new (one week at signal). A key caution: several top names carry FCF and earnings-basis overlays where filing, screen TTM, and company-adjusted figures diverge materially — quantitative passes on yield and growth screens should not be taken at face value without reconciling those definitions.

**FGP.L (FirstGroup plc)** — Ten of 22 models pass (composite 91%, sector-relative 86%), led by Earnings Yield (E/P 11.1%, P/E 9.0), Low P/E + High Yield (4.0% yield), Neff PEGY, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Composite Value, and Earnings Quality. ROE is 16.7% and net FCF dividend coverage is strong at 9.3×, but Graham-style screens fail on excessive leverage (D/E 161%), weak liquidity (current ratio 0.73), negative statutory earnings growth (-5.9%), and FCF Yield fails due to basis divergence (filing $362.6M vs screen TTM $302.8M vs company-adj £73.8M). Industrials concentration adds sector cyclicality alongside FGP. **Verdict: watchlist** — cheap on headline multiples with solid cash conversion, but leverage, liquidity, and unresolved FCF/earnings basis gaps warrant reconciliation before sizing a position.

**HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC)** — Ten of 22 models pass (composite 81%, sector-relative 91%), including Graham Enterprising, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, and Financial Health (D/E 77%, current ratio 1.82). Key metrics: P/E 12.7, P/B 1.9, yield 3.9%, ROE 15.4%. Failures include Earnings Yield (7.9% vs 8% threshold), FCF Yield (3.5% vs 5%), Piotroski F-Score (6/9), and Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion; net FCF dividend coverage 0.64×). Healthcare price-erosion overlay flagged filing pricing pressure despite quality/income passes. **Verdict: watchlist** — sector-relative cheapness and balance-sheet health are appealing, but weak cash conversion, negative statutory earnings growth (-4.7%), and the healthcare pricing overlay argue for patience.

**MEGP.L (ME Group International plc)** — Fifteen of 22 models pass (composite 83%, sector-relative 88%; highest model count in the group), including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield, Magic Formula, and Financial Health. Standout metrics: P/E 8.6, yield 6.9%, ROE 28.2%, D/E 28%, EV/EBIT 5.9. Interim-quality overlay notes interim EPS decline and net FCF/dividend coverage below 1.0× (gross 1.68×, net 0.84×). Piotroski F-Score 6/9 and Earnings Quality fail on weak free-cash conversion. Shares the Industrials cluster with FGP and MGNS. **Verdict: accumulate** — broadest quantitative confirmation in the top five with strong moat and cheapness signals, tempered by dividend sustainability at net coverage below 1×.

**ITV.L (ITV plc)** — Fourteen of 22 models pass (composite 78%, sector-relative 88%), including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG (PEG 0.45, growth 26.7%), Neff PEGY, Quality Value, High Dividend Yield (universe rank 97%), Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, and Financial Health. P/E 12.0, yield 7.0%, ROE 13.5%, D/E 52%; timing signal is "accumulate" (RSI 42, below 200-day MA). Piotroski F-Score is a weak 3/9 (ROA, OCF>NI, leverage, margins all deteriorating), and FCF basis diverges (filing $148M vs screen TTM $211.9M vs company-adj £325M). **Verdict: accumulate** — favourable entry timing and strong income/growth combo, but only after stress-testing whether the 7.0% yield is sustainable given weak F-Score and net FCF/dividend coverage of 0.79×.

**MGNS.L (Morgan Sindall Group plc)** — Sixteen of 22 models pass (composite 77%, sector-relative 80%; only name retaining unadjusted Strong Buy), spanning Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield (6.9%), Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG (PEG 0.61, growth 18.8%), Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Earnings Quality, and Financial Health (D/E 18%, coverage 53.9×). P/E 11.5, ROE 26.1%, net FCF dividend coverage 2.59×; no FCF or earnings basis overlay flagged. Economic Moat fails on thin margins and ROA below 8%. Third Industrials name in the top five. **Verdict: accumulate** — cleanest quantitative profile in the group with growth, cash flow, and balance-sheet alignment, though construction cyclicality remains a sector-level risk.

- FGP.L: High leverage (D/E 161%) and weak liquidity (current ratio 0.73) are not typical for a defensive transport operator; open question on lease-adjusted debt and pension obligations not captured in the screen.
- FGP.L: Statutory earnings growth -5.9% vs adjusted EPS growth +16% — sign divergence suggests one-off or accounting adjustments; governance around earnings presentation is an open question.
- FGP.L: FCF basis mismatch (filing $362.6M, company-adj £73.8M) — open question on whether reported cash generation is recurring or inflated by working-capital timing.
- HIK.L: Healthcare price-erosion overlay indicates filing pricing pressure — US/generic drug pricing regulation and pipeline concentration risk are not quantified in the screen.
- HIK.L: Net FCF dividend coverage 0.64× with heavy capex ($317M vs OCF $436M) — cyclicality of injectables/generics demand and R&D pipeline gaps are open questions.
- HIK.L: Leverage rising (Piotroski leverage-declining component failed) — balance-sheet trajectory under pricing pressure warrants scrutiny.
- MEGP.L: Interim EPS declined with net FCF/dividend coverage 0.84× on a 6.9% yield — open question on whether photo-booth/vending revenue is durable or tied to discretionary consumer/travel spend.
- MEGP.L: Statutory EPS growth +4.5% vs screen earnings growth -3.9% — earnings basis inconsistency; governance and segment disclosure quality unknown from screen data.
- ITV.L: Piotroski F-Score 3/9 with deteriorating ROA, margins, and leverage — structural decline in linear TV advertising and streaming competition risk not captured quantitatively.
- ITV.L: 7.0% yield with net FCF/dividend coverage 0.79× and OCF down from $333M to $202M YoY — dividend cut or rebasing risk is a material open question.
- ITV.L: FCF basis spans $148M to £325M company-adjusted — regulatory/media-licence obligations and content-commitment liabilities not in screen.
- MGNS.L: Construction/industrial contracting cyclicality — UK public-sector spending, housing pipeline, and margin compression in downturns are not modelled despite thin-margin Economic Moat failure.
- MGNS.L: ROA below 8% despite high ROE — asset-intensity and project write-down risk in a cyclical downturn are open questions.
- MGNS.L: Pension deficit and subcontractor liability exposure — insufficient data in JSON to assess; flag as open question.

question_outcomes.evidence: With 61 filing bodies now available (was 16), primary interim and trading-update extracts confirm a mixed durability picture rather than a pure discretionary vending business. H1 FY2026 (`filings/bodies/ir_3f2f55026f8c6fe6.txt`) reports diluted EPS down 3.9% to 6.48p, cash generated from operations £38.7m (−18.9%), capex £33.9m (implied gross FCF ~£4.8m), interim dividend cut to 3.60p (£13.5m), and net cash falling to £7.5m — well below 1.0× half-year cash dividend coverage versus the screen’s 0.84× net coverage on a full-year filing basis. Photo.ME still contributed 54.3% of H1 vending revenue but only 47.7% of Group EBITDA; Wash.ME reached 53.9% of EBITDA. The June trading update (`filings/bodies/ir_8a1ddede4c8b6528.txt`, `e5f6ebdd46934d00.txt`) links April Photo.ME weakness (−17% in April vs −6% for H1) to reduced demand for official photo ID amid travel uncertainty, while the annual report (`ir_a006e8bd9b660a9c.txt`) describes ID products as needs-driven but flags recession risk to discretionary spend, and separately cites stable cash flows from the established photobooth estate. Management states photobooth demand has partially recovered since April but is not expected to return to prior levels while travel uncertainty persists. No filing body quantifies fun-photo versus official ID revenue split — durability of the legacy photobooth cash engine remains inferred, not measured.

documents.name: FirstGroup plc
documents.executive_summary:
FirstGroup is a UK-focused bus and rail operator that has completed a multi-year pivot from North American disposal to a cleaner, UK-centric earnings base built on First Bus growth, open-access rail, and DfT management-fee contracts. The quantitative screen flags Strong Buy on cheapness (P/E ~9.0, earnings yield ~11%), dividend yield (~4.0%), and quality markers (Piotroski F-Score 8/9, ROE 16.7%), with five factor families passing. FY 2026 adjusted EPS rose to 20.3p (from 19.4p) despite a marginally lower adjusted operating profit, supported by buybacks and portfolio diversification including First Bus London. The valuation hook is a cash-generative business trading below 10x earnings with a progressive dividend and active capital return, but the key debate is whether accelerated bus electrification capex, rising adjusted net debt, and the structural transition of DfT rail contracts to public ownership leave reported free cash flow and earnings quality durable enough to justify the screen’s strong signal — especially given flagged FCF and earnings-basis divergences.

---
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, FirstGroup offers a rare combination in UK transport: visible adjusted earnings growth, shareholder returns, and a balance sheet that management targets below 2.0x adjusted net debt to adjusted EBITDA, without the legacy North American overhang. The screen’s Strong Buy rating is anchored in earnings yield, low P/E plus yield, Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, and Composite Value passes — a broad cheapness and quality cluster rather than a single metric. Business quality has improved materially: FY 2025 adjusted revenue was £1,370.0m with adjusted operating profit of £222.8m and adjusted EPS of 19.4p (FY 2025 results presentation); FY 2026 advanced to adjusted revenue of £1,718.7m, adjusted EPS of 20.3p, and total dividend of 7.2p (Companies House annual accounts, filed August 2026). Management is executing a disciplined capital allocation framework — progressive dividends (~3x adjusted EPS cover, tightening toward 2.5x), buybacks (£50m completed H1 2026; £100m programme launched June 2026), and bolt-on M&A — while repositioning earnings toward franchised bus, open-access rail, and Rail Services. The Piotroski score of 8/9 and dividend growth screen pass support the quality overlay, even as Graham-style and FCF-yield screens fail on leverage, liquidity, and FCF definition mismatch. Net: the screen correctly identifies a statistically cheap, improving UK transport compounder; deep research confirms the directional case but flags transition risk and accounting/FCF complexity that the screen partially adjusts for.

---
documents.financial_review:
**Primary sources:** FY 2026 results RNS (`filings/bodies/3bf5ff09fbc5c747.txt`), H1 2026 interim (`ir_032b08900a650e14.txt`, `c1db8cdf5ad2bd84.txt`), pre-close update (`4c56aaf324fdfd91.txt`), FY 2025 results presentation (`ir_5ba5b17047f87036.txt`). Yahoo used only for cross-check.

### Annual trend (FY 2025 → FY 2026)

| Metric | FY 2025 (filings) | FY 2026 (filings) | Note |
|--------|-------------------|-------------------|------|
| Adjusted revenue | £1,370.0m | £1,715.7m | +25% |
| Adjusted operating profit | £222.8m | £219.4m | Marginally lower |
| Adjusted earnings | £115.8m | £112.6m | −2.8% |
| Adjusted EPS | 19.4p | 20.3p | Buyback-driven (+4.6%) |
| Statutory/basic EPS | 21.3p | 21.4p | Flat |
| Dividend | 6.5p | 7.2p | +11% |
| Adjusted net debt | £86.9m | £137.7m | Higher |
| Company FCF (pre-acq/returns) | £113.5m | £73.8m | Lower (bus capex) |
| Statutory OCF | £828.2m | £681.5m | Lower |
| Capex (cash) | £156.4m | £253.0m | Electrification |

FY 2026 drivers: First Bus revenue **£1,443.6m** (+33%), adjusted OP **£102.8m** (+7%); First Rail adjusted OP **£129.9m** (−13%) on SWR transfer, open-access mobilisation, normalised DfT fees. Open-access revenue **£109.3m**. No adjusting items in FY 2026 (FY 2025 included Greyhound/pension settlement items per filing).

### Earnings basis reconciliation (gap-fill)

The screen’s statutory **−5.9%** earnings growth reflects **Yahoo net income**, not filing EPS (statutory EPS flat at 21.4p). Adjusted EPS growth is **+4.6%** full-year (not +16%, which is H1-only). Adjusted earnings declined; EPS growth is **mechanical from ~7% share reduction**, not operating leverage — a governance presentation point, not a FY 2026 one-off.

### FCF reconciliation (gap-fill)

| Basis | FY 2026 figure | Definition |
|-------|----------------|------------|
| Company-adjusted | **£73.8m** | Divisional EBITDA bridge; before acquisitions (£35.3m), dividends, buybacks |
| Yahoo OCF − capex | **~$362.6m / ~£273m** | Statutory consolidated; USD; excludes lease-debt service |
| Screen TTM | **$302.8m** | Suppressed; quarterly cashflow unavailable |

FY 2026 working capital contributed **+£14.6m** to operations — FCF was **not** inflated by year-end WC timing. First Bus FCF was only **£10.5m** after **£188.2m** electrification capex; H1 had **£(35.6)m** outflow. Management guides **~£400m** cumulative FCF over three years (TOC cash unwind, capex normalising to **£80–100m** from FY 2028).

**Dividend coverage:** On company FCF **£73.8m** vs dividends paid **£38.9m** ≈ **1.9×** net coverage. Screen’s **9.3×** uses Yahoo filing-aligned FCF and overstates sustainability.

### Balance sheet (gap-fill)

| Metric | FY 2026 | Interpretation |
|--------|---------|----------------|
| Adjusted net debt | £137.7m | Management KPI; ex-IFRS 16, ex-ring-fenced cash |
| Reported net debt | £725.3m | Includes IFRS 16 |
| IFRS 16 lease liabilities | £850.0m | Drives headline leverage |
| Ring-fenced cash | £260.8m | DfT TOC liquidity |
| Pre-IFRS 16 net cash (bonds/bank) | (£124.7m) | Underlying bank debt modest |
| Screen D/E 161% | Yahoo | **Includes leases**; not comparable to adjusted net debt |
| Current ratio 0.73 | Yahoo | Structural for transport (working-capital-negative) |
| Undrawn RCF | £295.0m | Liquidity buffer |

Leverage policy: **<2.0× adjusted net debt : Rail adjusted EBITDA**. Covenant detail **not in corpus** — open gap.

### Interim and trading update (unchanged, filing-confirmed)

H1 FY 2026: adjusted revenue **£833.6m**, adjusted EPS **9.9p**, adjusted net debt **£207.6m**, FCF **£(35.6)m**. Pre-close (26 March 2026): trading in line; year-end adjusted net debt **£135–145m**.

**Remaining gaps:** IFRS 16 maturity ladder; RCF covenant headroom note; FY 2026 results presentation PDF not ingested; Mistral disposal (£48m, ~£46m gain as adjusting item) forward impact from headline-only RNS.

---
documents.risks_and_flags:
**Evidenced (filings)**

- **Accounting / governance:** Multiple non-GAAP definitions (adjusted revenue, adjusted earnings ex-IFRS 16 on DfT TOCs, company FCF). FY 2026 had **zero adjusting items**, yet adjusted EPS rose while adjusted earnings fell — buyback-driven optics. Prior-year levy reclassification (£167.6m revenue/expense, nil P&L impact) shows comparability care needed.
- **Leverage (headline):** Screen D/E **161%** is **IFRS 16-inclusive** (Yahoo); not indicative of distress on management’s **£137.7m adjusted net debt**, but lease stack **£850m** is structurally real.
- **Liquidity:** Current ratio **0.73** (Yahoo); **£295m** undrawn RCF and going-concern confirmation to September 2027 (FY 2026 results RNS).
- **FCF / capex:** Company FCF **£73.8m** is cyclically depressed by bus electrification; not recurring at Yahoo-implied levels. Dividend coverage **~1.9×** on company basis vs screen **9.3×** on Yahoo basis.
- **Regulatory:** DfT TOC renationalisation (GWR December 2026; WCP ~FY 2027 end); bus franchising; fare-cap policy.
- **Cyclical:** Regional bus volumes **−3%** FY 2026; commercial **−6%**; open-access yield pressure.
- **Pension:** Net surplus **£19.9m** at FY 2026; **~£65m** in escrow pending 2030 valuations.

**Still open (alternate source needed)**

- **Covenant risk:** RCF/facility covenants and headroom — **Annual Report borrowing note** or credit agreement summary.
- **Lease maturity concentration:** Maturity profile beyond totals — **IFRS 16 note / results presentation lease table**.
- **Forward FCF:** Mistral sale (July 2026 RNS headline) — full disposal RNS body for pro-forma FCF and adjusting-item treatment.

RiskTags: regulatory, cyclical, governance, pension, leverage, liquidity, accounting

---
documents.news_highlights:

**Strategy and contracts**

- “FirstGroup PLC (FGROF) Full Year 2026 Earnings Call Highlights: Strong Revenue Growth Amidst…” (Yahoo Finance, 20 June 2026) — cites ~25% revenue increase and £100m buyback.

- “FirstGroup plc Completes Share Buyback, Repurchasing 2.77 Million Shares at 179.85p Average Price” (Kalkine Media, 27 July 2026).

**Other**

- Numerous DirectorsTalk “40–55% upside potential” articles — promotional tone; not treated as fundamental news.

**Thin/ noisy areas:** Independent operational coverage is limited; bulk of Google News flow is repetitive bullish sell-side summaries. One Business Standard headline on “FGP standalone net profit” (August 2026) appears to reference a different entity and is disregarded.

weekly_updates.summary:
**Q: Statutory earnings growth -5.9% vs adjusted EPS growth +16% — sign divergence suggests one-off or accounting adjustments; governance around earnings presentation is an open question.**

**Status:** partially_resolved

**Evidence:** The FY 2026 results RNS body (`filings/bodies/3bf5ff09fbc5c747.txt`, 18 June 2026) states there were **no adjusting items in FY 2026**; statutory basic EPS was **21.4p** (FY 2025: **21.3p**, essentially flat), while adjusted EPS rose to **20.3p** (FY 2025: **19.4p**, +4.6%). Adjusted *earnings* actually fell to **£112.6m** from **£115.8m**; the EPS uplift is explained by the buyback (weighted average shares **553.4m** vs **597.7m**). The screen’s **-5.9% statutory growth** aligns with Yahoo net income decline (`financials_annual.json`: $127.5m → $118.3m), not filing statutory EPS; the screen’s **+16% adjusted growth** matches H1 interim (+16% to 9.9p), not full-year adjusted EPS (+4.6%).

**SourcesTried:** filings_bodies, filings_index, yahoo_financials, screening_snapshot, ir_presentation_metrics

**NextSources:** FY 2026 Annual Report note 4 adjusting-items policy and auditor APM commentary (`firstgroupplc.com` PDF); Companies House iXBRL income-statement taxonomy cross-check for Yahoo/Filing statutory net income bridge

**Q: FCF basis mismatch (filing $362.6M, company-adj £73.8M) — open question on whether reported cash generation is recurring or inflated by working-capital timing.**

**Status:** partially_resolved

**Evidence:** FY 2026 results RNS reconciles company FCF **£73.8m** as divisional bridge (Open access **£32.2m** + DfT TOCs **£67.5m** + First Bus **£10.5m** − Group **£36.4m**), derived from adjusted cash flow **£(124.0)m** plus add-backs for acquisitions (**£35.3m**), dividends (**£38.9m**), and buybacks (**£50.4m**). Cash from operations was **£681.5m** with a **£14.6m working-capital inflow** (not a year-end WC boost). Yahoo **$362.6m** = OCF **$615.6m** − capex **$253.0m** (`financials_annual.json`); it excludes the **£432.5m** lease-liability payments that sit in the company’s adjusted cash-flow waterfall and uses USD. H1 FCF was **£(35.6)m** (electrification capex **£188.2m** in FY 2026 full year for First Bus). Management guides **~£400m** FCF over three years as DfT TOC cash returns and bus capex normalise.

**SourcesTried:** filings_bodies, filings_index, yahoo_financials, yahoo_quarterly_cashflow, ir_presentation_metrics, screening_snapshot

**NextSources:** FY 2026 results presentation PDF FCF bridge slide (`firstgroupplc.com/investors`); quarterly cash-flow ingest to rebuild screen TTM ($302.8m currently suppressed with empty quarterly data)

**Q: What drives the gap between filing FCF ($362.6M), screen TTM ($302.8M), and company-adjusted FCF (£73.8M), and is the 160% D/E ratio lease-adjusted or indicative of structural balance-sheet risk?**

**Status:** partially_resolved

**Evidence:** Three definitions: (1) **Yahoo/filing-aligned $362.6m** = statutory OCF minus capex, USD, no lease-debt service; (2) **screen TTM $302.8m** = suppressed TTM (`financials_annual.json`: `ttm_cashflow_suppressed: true`, quarterly cashflow empty); (3) **company £73.8m** = management FCF before acquisitions/returns, after divisional working capital and **before** shareholder distributions. FY 2026 adjusted net debt **£137.7m** vs reported net debt **£725.3m**; IFRS 16 lease liabilities **£850.0m** and ring-fenced cash **£260.8m** (`3bf5ff09fbc5c747.txt`). Screen D/E **160.8%** uses Yahoo total debt **$1,005m** (includes **$850m** capital lease obligations) / equity **$710m** — **not lease-adjusted**. Management leverage target: **<2.0× adjusted net debt : Rail adjusted EBITDA**; covenant text not in available extracts.

**SourcesTried:** filings_bodies, filings_index, yahoo_financials, screening_snapshot, screen_run_manifest, ir_presentation_metrics

**NextSources:** Annual Report note on borrowing facilities and covenant headroom; IFRS 16 lease maturity schedule (partial totals only in `ir_presentation_metrics.json`: £1,203.6m FY 2025, £1,017.2m H1 2026 — no maturity ladder yet)

**Q: (FirstGroup plc) — Ten of 22 models pass… Verdict: watchlist — cheap on headline multiples with solid cash conversion, but leverage, liquidity, and unresolved FCF/earnings basis gaps warrant reconciliation before sizing a position.**

**Status:** partially_resolved

**Evidence:** Screen snapshot confirmed: **10/22** pass, composite **91%**, families cheapness/quality/dividend/GARP/risk; failures on Graham, FCF Yield (basis divergence), Financial Health (D/E, current ratio **0.73**), Lynch PEG (negative statutory earnings growth). Gap-fill now shows: cheapness on **adjusted EPS 20.3p / P/E ~9** is filing-supported; “solid cash conversion” is **mixed** — OCF strong (£681.5m) but company FCF **£73.8m** covers dividends ~**1.9×** (not the screen’s **9.3×** coverage, which uses Yahoo FCF). Adjusted net debt **£137.7m** is manageable on management metrics; headline D/E **161%** is structurally inflated by IFRS 16. documents.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
documents.executive_summary: Hikma is a diversified FTSE 100 generic and specialty pharmaceutical group spanning US injectables, MENA branded generics, and US oral/specialty (Hikma Rx), trading at roughly 12.7× P/E and 1.9× P/B with a ~3.9% dividend yield — metrics that underpin the quantitative **strong buy** (10/22 models, 81% composite, 91% sector-relative). The investment case rests on a quality compounder trading below historical multiples after a February 2026 guidance reset, now partially repaired by a solid H1 2026 beat and reiterated FY guidance. The central debate is whether Branded momentum and Hikma Rx mix improvement can offset structurally lower Injectables margins, elevated capex, and weak reported free cash flow ($119m FY2025; screen flags FCF basis divergence). Deep research broadly supports accumulation at current valuation, but overlays on earnings quality, healthcare pricing, and cash conversion warrant measured sizing rather than full conviction.
documents.investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen flags Hikma across five factor families — cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk — passing Graham Enterprising, Buffett Quality, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, and Financial Health, among others. At P/E 12.7, P/B 1.9, ROE 15.4%, and debt/equity 77%, the stock screens as inexpensive relative to a business with investment-grade balance sheet (BBB/stable, S&P and Fitch), 16% ROIC (FY2025 filing), and a growing dividend (84 cents FY2025, +5%).

Business quality is segment-differentiated. **Branded** is the standout: FY2025 core revenue +10%, core operating profit +19%, margin 26.4%; H1 2026 revenue +15%, core operating margin 32.5%, with Hikma the largest pharma company by sales in MENA. **Hikma Rx** is stabilising: FY2025 core revenue ~$1.04bn flat, margin 17.3% rising to 20.6% in H1 2026 on CMO mix and sodium oxybate terms. **Injectables** remains the swing factor: FY2025 core revenue +7% but core operating profit −6% (margin 31.0% vs 35.3%), with H1 2026 revenue flat and core margin 27.6%.

For a value investor, the hook is a credible recovery narrative — Said Darwazah's return as CEO (December 2025), withdrawal of medium-term margin guidance, increased Injectables investment, and a $250m share buyback signal management alignment — layered onto a stock that screens cheaply versus healthcare peers while paying an income stream with gross FCF dividend coverage of ~1.3× (net ~0.64× per screen). Failed screens (FCF Yield, Economic Moat, Piotroski 6/9, Earnings Quality) correctly flag that the cheapness is not pristine; the thesis requires Branded to keep compounding while Injectables margins floor in the guided 27–28% range.

documents.name: ME Group International plc
documents.executive_summary:
ME Group International plc (MEGP.L) operates a global estate of ~49,000 self-service vending units—chiefly photobooths (Photo.ME) and unattended laundry (Wash.ME)—across 16 countries, with long-dated site contracts in high-footfall locations. The quantitative screen rates the name a strong buy (15/22 models; composite 83%; P/E 8.6×, yield 6.9%, ROE 28.2%, debt/equity 28%), reflecting cheapness, quality cash generation, and dividend support against a business mixing mature photobooth cash flows with fast-growing laundry.

The valuation hook is a market pricing ME Group as a declining photobooth operator, while filings show laundry now contributing 46% of FY2025 EBITDA and strategic contracts (ASDA, SNCF, RATP) expanding the installed base. FY2025 delivered record profit before tax of £78.2m on £315.4m revenue, with cash generated from operations of £115.5m and net cash of £26.5m.

The central debate is whether near-term cyclical and regulatory pressure on photobooths—and a revised FY2026 PBT guidance of £69–74m—are transitory, or whether they reveal structural limits to the “value plus growth” narrative. Accounting restatements (cash-in-transit), a delayed FY2025 audit, and an interim dividend cut add governance friction that the screen does not fully capture.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, ME Group presents a rare combination: statistically cheap on earnings and yield, operationally profitable (EBITDA margin 38.2% in FY2025), and self-funded for growth. The screen passes five factor families—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk—with high data quality (20/20 metrics). Filing-aligned free cash flow of £25.2m (FY2025 operating cash flow £90.8m after capex of £65.6m) supports an earnings-yield and FCF-yield case that is not purely accounting-based.

Business quality rests on durable competitive positioning: dominant photobooth share, high barriers to entry, no customer above 2% of turnover, and multi-year contracts with site owners. Wash.ME is the growth engine—1,145 net laundry units added in FY2025, EBITDA up 18.1% to £55.5m—and is reshaping the mix toward higher-return capital deployment. Management is returning capital (FY2025 dividend £32.6m; £18m buyback launched March 2026) while maintaining net cash.

The screen’s strong-buy signal aligns with FY2025 filing fundamentals. The adjusted “buy” overlay (interim EPS decline; net FCF/dividend coverage 0.84×) is directionally correct: the equity remains attractive on trailing numbers, but H1 FY2026 confirms that earnings momentum has slowed and capital returns are competing with heavy reinvestment. For a patient value holder, the asymmetry lies in buying a cash-generative franchise at single-digit earnings multiples while laundry scale and new partnerships (ASDA targeting up to 700 UK machines) compound; the screen’s cheapness and quality passes are well grounded in primary filings, not Yahoo proxies.

documents.risks_and_flags:
**Evidenced (post 61-body refetch):**

- **Cyclical / consumer (Photo.ME):** Trading update (`ir_8a1ddede4c8b6528.txt`) attributes April photobooth weakness to official photo ID demand and travel uncertainty; interim (`ir_3f2f55026f8c6fe6.txt`) states recovery is partial and not expected to reach prior levels while travel uncertainty persists. Annual risk table (`ir_a006e8bd9b660a9c.txt`) explicitly links recession to discretionary spend, mitigated by needs-driven ID positioning — confirming hybrid exposure.
- **Regulatory (Photo.ME):** German and Japanese ID rule changes remain structural headwinds; next-gen biometric rollout H2 FY2026 per interim filing.
- **Dividend / liquidity:** FY net FCF/dividend 0.84×; H1 cash coverage ~0.33× on dividends paid. Net cash £7.5m at April 2026 after capex, dividends, tax, and buybacks. Interim dividend cut is management’s visible response; simultaneous £18m buyback (`1d660d1c237711ac.txt`) increases payout competition with reinvestment.

rules: Universe: only strong_buy / buy names from the latest screen.
Timing filter: names with timing_signal=wait are excluded from new buys.
Sector cap: at most 1 name(s) per known sector (cap=20%).
Ranking: highest conviction_score first, keep at most 3 names.
Sizing: equal-weight sleeves of current NAV after exits; buys limited by remaining cash.
Costs: 3.0% applied on each buy and sell.
Hold buffer: full exit only after 2 consecutive rebalance(s) outside the target set.
Re-entry cooldown: wait 1 rebalance(s) after a full exit before buying the same name again.
Dust guard: skip trim/top-up adjustments below £10.

question_outcomes.question: Healthcare price-erosion overlay indicates filing pricing pressure — US/generic drug pricing regulation and pipeline concentration risk are not quantified in the screen.
question_outcomes.evidence: Re-read of 58 filing bodies confirms overlay trigger language in `ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt` ("expected price erosion across the base portfolio"; "usual price erosion"; US competition on testosterone/calcitonin), `ir_a70365d580129295.txt` ("Increased competition on higher margin products"; "price erosion"), and `5f26e81d036b3596.txt` ("modest price erosion across the portfolio, in line with recent history"). H1 principal risks define **Market dynamics and commercial environment** to include "pricing and reimbursement environments, regulatory and policy interventions" and flag increased exposure to potential US generic import tariffs (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`). Quantified margin impact: Injectables core margin guided **27–28%** for 2026 vs **31.0%** FY2025 (`94eb1f8d38a51fa6.txt`). Pipeline breadth: **300+ products**, **84 launches in 2025** (`ir_3a67962eb8770824.txt`); **118 injectables pipeline products** in FY2025 release (`ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt`). Generic pricing **antitrust MDL** bellwether September 2026 — liability "impracticable to estimate" (`ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt`). No CMS/IQVIA quantification in local sources.
